title: Spare Bedroom Ideas: Smart Ways to Use an Extra Room
h1: Spare Bedroom Ideas: Smart Ways to Use an Extra Bedroom, From Guest Room Office Combos to Home Gyms
description: Spare bedroom ideas for apartments: guest room office combos, home gyms, dressing rooms and more, with room sizes, layout tips, and typical budgets.
secondary_keywords: what to do with a spare room
excerpt: Turn an underused second bedroom into a guest room office combo, home gym, dressing room or studio, with sizes, layouts and budgets.
image_alt: Spare bedroom ideas shown in a guest room office combo with a daybed, a wooden desk by the window, and wall shelves
key_takeaways: Design the spare room for how you use it most weeks, then build in the occasional use.
A daybed, sleeper sofa, or Murphy bed makes a guest room office combo work without crowding the desk.
Keep at least 30 inches of clearance between the desk chair and the bed, including with a sleeper opened.
Closed storage lets the room switch between uses in minutes.
Give the spare room its own palette, lighting, and textiles so it feels intentional, not leftover.

faq.q: What can I do with a spare bedroom?
faq.a: Popular uses include a guest room, a guest room office combo, a dedicated home office, a home gym, a dressing room or walk-in closet, a hobby or craft studio, a reading room, or a media den. Choose based on how you will use the room most weeks, not just a few times a year when guests visit.

faq.q: How do you combine a guest room and home office?
faq.a: Choose a sleeping option that does not dominate the room, such as a daybed, sleeper sofa, or Murphy bed. Place the desk near the window and the bed on the longest wall, with at least 30 inches between them. Add closed storage so you can hide work materials and clear space for guests quickly.

faq.q: What size bed fits in a small spare bedroom?
faq.a: A twin daybed (about 39 x 75 inches) fits almost any spare room and doubles as seating. A full bed (54 x 75 inches) needs roughly a 9 x 10 foot room to leave walkways. A queen (60 x 80 inches) generally needs at least 10 x 10 feet to feel comfortable with nightstands.

faq.q: How do I make a spare room feel welcoming for guests?
faq.a: Invest in a good mattress and layered bedding, add a lamp and surface on each side of the bed, and provide blackout curtains, a mirror, empty hangers, and a luggage rack. Small touches such as fresh towels, a written Wi-Fi password, a carafe of water, and a charger near the bed make a big difference.

faq.q: Is it worth turning a spare bedroom into a home gym?
faq.a: If you train at home three or more times a week, a dedicated room lets you leave equipment set up and saves time. Use rubber flooring to protect floors and reduce noise, add a mirror and good ventilation, and choose compact equipment. In apartments, consider weight limits and noise for neighbors below.
